newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bribery scandal brings down South Korean minister.
newsitem.headline: Bribery scandal brings down South Korean minister.

text.p: South Korea's health minister stepped down on Wednesday in the second bribery scandal to rock the cabinet and embarrass President Kim Young-sam in less than a month.
Lee Sung-ho, Minister of Health and Welfare, quit amid reports in the state media that his wife had accepted a 160 million won ($193,000) payment from an opticians' trade association.
Hours after the announcement of his resignation, Lee appeared for questioning at the Seoul prosecutor's office.
No charges have been brought against Lee, and he has not made any public statement.
Last month Kim sacked his defence minister, Lee Yang-ho, who was formally charged on Monday with accepting bribes and leaking state secrets.

The scandals are a double blow to Kim who has staked his reputation as an anti-corruption campaigner and whose drive to clean up South Korean society has brought to justice former presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
A presidential Blue House statement said the health minister resigned "because his wife was suspected of taking bribes".
"I feel bitter over this incident," Kim was quoted as saying. "In the future I will not condone anybody who is linked to corruption, regardless of whether their title is high or low."

State-run Korea Broadcasting System quoted unnamed prosecutors as saying Lee's wife, Park Sung-ae, was taken in for questioning on Tuesday night and had confessed to accepting 160 million won from the Korean Optometric Association.
The association was seeking changes in the law to give members a monopoloy over the sale of spectacle frames, the television report said.
An official at the optometric association declined to comment on the charges.
President Kim appointed a member of parliament for the ruling New Korea party, Sohn Hak-kyu, as his new health chief, the Blue House statement said.
"Kim Young-sam appointed Sohn Hak-kyu because he believes he is clean and able," the statement said.
"Since Kim's inauguration he has put emphasis on rooting out corruption and setting up morality and cleanliness among public officers," it added. Kim took office in 1993.
Former defence minister Lee was fired on October 17, hours before allegations that he received illicit pay-offs surfaced in the National Assembly.

Lee Yang-ho was charged with taking 150 million won as part of his share of payments to an American-Korean arms dealer from Daewoo Heavy Industries in connection with a military purchase of helicopters.
The former head of Daewoo Heavy, Sok Chin-chol, was also indicted along with two employees of the arms merchant.
Former president Roh is now appealing a 22-1/2 year jail sentence for bribery, treason and mutiny. His predecessor Chun is trying to escape a death sentence on similar charges.

A corruption scandal is also swirling around Seoul city hall after two senior municipal officials were arrested last month for allegedly accepting a total of 39 million won in bribes from city bus operators.
